reviews.text: Everything about this is so clichéd and simply ludicrous it’s not even worth watching on a plane. It’s another drivel featuring Dwayne Johnson as another stolid, banal hero.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: I found “San Andreas” to be entertaining in its own cheesy, summer blockbustery way.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: While its entire reason for being is to supply a bankable, familiar product that will deliver extensive returns, we can feel safe in the knowledge that a movie like San Andreas will not test our limits and will quickly disappear from our thoughts.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: San Andreas is a mixed landscape  unfortunately more shaky than not.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: One can't exactly hate a film that delivers all the empty sound-and-fury stimuli it promises, but no matter the expense and excess, it still all adds up to just a glut of expensive... emptiness.
reviews.author: Michael Dequina

reviews.text: Peyton's panoramas of crumbling CGI skyscrapers are spectacular but repetitive, and the script by Carlton Cuse (Lost) is uneven and cheesy.
reviews.author: Nick Levine

reviews.text: San Andreas plays like a greatest hits package of action movies from the past quarter-century.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: I hoped the ground would open up and gobble up whole the movie. What a disaster.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: There's not a lot to hold onto in San Andreas. It ticks the boxes of a disaster film, but rarely, if ever, asks the audience to do anything other than ooh and ahh at its effects.
reviews.author: Craig Schroeder

reviews.text: Unfolds exactly like a Roland Emmerich disaster movie, which means the screen is awash with computer-enhanced destruction of epic proportions.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: This is the type of natural disaster for which Westboro Baptist Church and Pat Robertson would surely blame those silly Californian liberals.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: I was pleasantly surprised. This is a highly entertaining disaster film. It's a scary, pulse-pounding thrill ride...also emotional without getting overly schmaltzy, which is difficult for a lot of movies to accomplish, let alone an action film.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: Sheer, utter absurdity on every level.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: If I called San Andreas "a huge disaster." director Brad Peyton would probably take it as a compliment. It's not a compliment.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: Screenwriter Carlton Cuse delivers an interesting script, but somewhere in the passing of the torch to director Brad Peyton, how-much-CGI-can-we-use clearly became the overriding production mantra which then detracted from the raw human drama and emotion.
reviews.author: Debbie Lynn Elias

reviews.text: It's not dumb often enough. Combine that with a lead character who abandons his appointed life-saving duties at the precise moment he's most needed, and you have an uneven flick that flirts with disaster more than embraces it.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: San Andreas falls into the disaster porn trap of giving us only a few characters to follow while they're otherwise surrounded by hordes of screaming destruction fodder.
reviews.author: Josh Goller

reviews.text: San Andreas is a popcorn munching, soda-pop slurping feast of thrilling silliness.
reviews.author: Christopher Preston

reviews.text: It feels stale and the sideplots aren't very engaging.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: So schematic and simplistic in its dramatic framework as it is fantastic and amazing in its graphic and physical embodiment of the devastating effects of the cataclysm. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Fernandez

reviews.text: The script of San Andrés is as simple and schematic as that of most disaster films, except that it is more honest: it does not need a dozen characters to fill in the story.
reviews.author: Quim Casas

reviews.text: An entertainment as stupid as it is splendid, which never wanes in almost two hours of footage. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio Benítez

reviews.text: San Andreas is just one kill away from being pretty good. If just one of the main five characters had died, it would have made a world of difference.
reviews.author: Bernard Boo

reviews.text: Per San Andreas, if the big one hits, just sit back, cross your fingers, and wish the Rock was your dad.
reviews.author: Zaki Hasan

reviews.text: Sure, there is plenty of carnage, but there is more talking -- not the best idea when your film's biggest draw is watching stuff get destroyed.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: If you have been hoping for a new disaster flick with maximum amount of devastation this fits the bill in spades.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: It's more of a Saturday night, stay-in-and-eat-pizza type of movie, and even then you might end up watching one of its many contemporaries instead and not notice the difference.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: San Andreas should be judged exactly for what it is: A fast-paced disaster film with engaging performances and exhilarating set-pieces of destruction.
reviews.author: Aaron Peterson

reviews.text: The earth rubs its tectonic plates together real good, and even if you can see the end coming, it's a helluva ride getting there.
reviews.author: Pat Padua

reviews.text: San Andreas is a visual assault on the eyes and ears for its entire 112 minutes running time that leaves you thinking the disaster was in making the film.
reviews.author: Rosalynn Try-Hane

reviews.text: The movie is soulless, having exchanged its soul with cheap thrills and corny melodrama.
reviews.author: Oggs Cruz

reviews.text: 'San Andreas' is the kind of movie one sees with the biggest bag of popcorn available; it's pure and simple escapism, fun without pretensions. Watch it in 3D, and watch it with little expectations, and you'll have a good time. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Another genre, another set of shameless clichés. San Andreas is, nevertheless, a much more enjoyable film.
reviews.author: Camilla Long

reviews.text: If you are going to sell audiences a disaster movie starring The Rock, it's probably not wise to have him flying a helicopter doing nothing for the majority of the running time
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: The end result might be a melange of scenes taken from other films, but in a summer season groaning with sci-fi and superhero sequels, this survival epic must be given credit for striking out on its own.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: ... San Andreas is perfectly acceptable mindless weekend cable fare.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: The plot is implausible and the situations even more preposterous.
reviews.author: Joanne Soh

reviews.text: There is a lot here that is absolutely atrocious and yet it is entirely enjoyable throughout.
reviews.author: Amanda Keats

reviews.text: At least if the big one does hit, we can't say nobody warned us.
reviews.author: Sr. Rose Pacatte

reviews.text: This adrenaline-pumping movie turns a nightmare into big screen reality as it takes the disaster film genre to a whole new level.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: Heaven help me, I had a great time.
reviews.author: Jeff Simon

reviews.text: San Andreas turns horror on an unimaginable scale into light entertainment. Pass the popcorn!
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: All the moving parts are expertly juggled by director Brad Peyton and, yes, the special effects are impressive. But the disaster stuff is laid on way too thick.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: Maybe, if this film has any purpose at all, it's to make us stop for a moment and think about the reality.
reviews.author: Francesca Rudkin

reviews.text: Empty, cynical destruction porn that's twice as dumb as it should be and not half as enjoyable.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: San Andreas typifies the modern Hollywood disaster movie - for better and for worse. The visuals are quite something, but it's all a bit hollow and there's little satisfaction in its conclusions.
reviews.author: Marija Djurovic

reviews.text: It's an unintentionally comedic look at mankind's selfish disinterest toward anyone in danger -- except for family.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Best Performance by a Semi-Retired Professional Wrestler in an Irwin Allen-styled Disaster Movie? That'll be the day I go back to Annandale...
reviews.author: David N. Butterworth

reviews.text: So, I suppose, I would recommend this movie, provided you know exactly what you're getting yourself into.
reviews.author: Kyle Anderson

reviews.text: Who'd have thought that the demise of several cities full of unnamed people would act as a perverse sort of marriage counselling for a couple in nuptial distress?
reviews.author: Matt Wolf

reviews.text: The plot, the beats, the character arcs? They all seem like they come from a Hollywood build-your-own-disaster movie kit.
reviews.author: David Blaustein

reviews.text: It's enormously entertaining, thanks to the undeniable charisma of Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson and the wanton CGI destruction of all of the West Coast's greatest landmarks (in 3-D, no less).
reviews.author: Sophie Gilbert

reviews.text: What Johnson does best, probably better than anyone else right now, is to draw attention to the absurdity, even the impossibility of himself. In a movie so invested on making him seem possible, that performance, so endearing and so smart, gets lost.
reviews.author: Cynthia Fuchs

reviews.text: Summer's upon us, and you could do worse than watch the undeniably appealing Johnson try to save the day while uttering the silliest dialogue imaginable.
reviews.author: Jocelyn Noveck

reviews.text: You could certainly do worse and should be entertained enough, despite its many faults.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: How much you enjoy the movie depends on how much mass destruction you can deal with and how much cheese you can stomach.
reviews.author: Nick Dent

reviews.text: The main problem is that the film can't decide whether it wants to be a proper disaster movie or a Dwayne Johnson action vehicle.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: San Andreas is nowhere near the best movie made this year. Indeed, it might be one of the worst. But it is, without a doubt, one of the most unapologetic, self-aware, and entertaining romps of 2015. And that counts for something.
reviews.author: Alex Abad-Santos

reviews.text: San Andreas picks its humans so carefully, it starts to feel Calvinist in its approach to salvation as Ray Gaines becomes deus ex heli, using the taxpayers' equipment to save his own family.
reviews.author: Katherine Monk

reviews.text: This movie didn't take much time escalating from realistic depiction of a disaster to giant, numbing CGI spectacle.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: San Andreas may have impressive special effects, but without a well-developed human element or an emotional core, it becomes a rather empty experience that fails to pull the audience into its tale of epic destruction.
reviews.author: Jeff Beck

reviews.text: Delivers what it promises: unrelenting entertainment and pure action. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mario P. Székely

reviews.text: Earthquakes hit California, and The Rock teams up with his estranged wife to save their daughter. That's pretty much it, and that's all there really needs to be.
reviews.author: Josh Terry

reviews.text: There are a couple of nice shots, including one of a BART hurtling out of its tunnel and another of a naval vessel wedged between two skyscrapers, seemingly lifted straight from the concept art, but the real order of business here is destruction.
reviews.author: Clem Bastow

reviews.text: Propelled by a continuing series of quakes spread out over the entire state, San Andreas is all forward momentum and non-stop action, but with enough narrative focus to avoid letting the calamity totally engulf the picture.
reviews.author: Steve Biodrowski

reviews.text: It's clear from the get-go that the filmmakers have more commercial than creative motives here, and their plot has the cracks to prove it.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: San Andreas stands out as a better-than-average endeavor that, at the very least, boasts one of Johnson's most charismatic performances to date.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: Director Brad Peyton keeps the story focused on a handful of compelling, resourceful people to keep us rooting for their survival while they race through increasingly complex set pieces.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: By the end--a seismologist told "You did good" as reports come in of California's devastation and corpse-littered cities--it's clear just how tone-deaf, context-insensitive, and death-denying this blockbuster is after all its bombast and bomb-blasts.
reviews.author: Brian Gibson

reviews.text: Set up as an old-style disaster movie with only a fraction of the plot, this earthquake action adventure is preposterous enough to just about work as a guilty pleasure.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: If you're caught in a movie between a rock and a hard place, choose the Rock every time.
reviews.author: Steve Persall

reviews.text: ...dispenses with ridiculous complications like those employed in 2012 and The Day After Tomorrow. This is a pure popcorn flick sanitized for family viewing: enjoy and forget.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: A mindless, over the top plot with equally over the top performances from everybody involved. [full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mabel Salinas

reviews.text: It doesn't hurt to drop the intellectual pose and let yourself enjoy a good old destruction movie. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Oscar Rodríguez

reviews.text: Completely unrealistic. [full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: It's not The Rock's fault.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: its disaster spectacle and sense of moral reckoning is hung on exactly the same narrative backbone as Emmerich's world-shattering "2012"
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: When a foolish woman separates from the world's manliest man in favor of a cowardly architect who builds wobbly skyscrapers that rudely scrape the heavens, is it any wonder the angry gods smite her home state from top to bottom?
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: Preposterously effective special effects and almost tolerable storylines.
reviews.author: Bruce Bennett

reviews.text: a whiz-bang of a disaster flick brimming over with close-calls, near misses, and the answer to that age-old question, "What would a cruise ship drifting through Chinatown look like?"
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: It's a snooze enlivened by regular orgies of heavy stuff falling on people.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: A disaster movie that isn't a complete disaster. This one offers up some great special effects that compensate for some of the story's sillier moments.
reviews.author: John Hanlon

reviews.text: It's dumb, but at least it has a smile plastered on its face the whole way through.
reviews.author: Alex Doenau

reviews.text: Say what you will, the movie is critic-proof, and even the most cynical will have to admit it delivers what you bought your ticket to see.
reviews.author: Jim Lane

reviews.text: My resistance to summer blockbusters crumbled like a collapsing skyscraper in the face of this big, loud, exuberantly destructive movie.
reviews.author: J. R. Jones

reviews.text: As disaster epics go, "San Andreas" works. ... It's not genius filmmaking, but it's undemandingly entertaining.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Exactly the movie you suppose it to be, except in one, absolutely crucial regard: it's weirdly allergic to fun.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: I was in the mood for a big, dumb disaster movie when I saw this, and this one delivers on both counts. A lot of time is spent on feelings and relationships in this movie. This is like a Jane Austen earthquake disaster movie.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Has a massive heart and makes the right choices at the right moments, and manages to skilfully avoid the many inherent pitfalls with this sort of material.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: Sets out to prove that The Rock can go toe-to-toe with two earthquakes and a tsunami and come out on top by the sheer power of his biceps and a helpful screenwriter.
reviews.author: Ken Hanke

reviews.text: Visually well-executed, shiny and seat-rattling, and completely useless otherwise. It does the one thing it set out to do, though, and so here we are.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: Campy but never campy enough and far too numbingly artificial to ever drum up any real suspense or sense of awe, the film has a scale that's squandered on visual witlessness.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: The allure of San Andreas rests entirely on the calibre of its pandemonium, savored, ideally, with a brawling audience on a Friday night.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: At least marks a technological progression from the days when directors of earthquake movies just shook the camera and dropped painted chunks of Styrofoam on the set.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: There's nothing here to shake off genre clichés or provide added marquee value.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: Another green-screen spectacle that demands you turn your brains off at the same time you turn off your mobile phone... a terrific popcorn time-killer...[but] pitted with way too many plot holes and movie coincidences.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Big, Dumb and Fun' should almost be its own genre by now, and San Andreas is nothing but.
reviews.author: Tom Glasson

reviews.text: The lack of acting and screenplay is hardly a bump in the road for this hyperventilating 3D quake-a-palooza.
reviews.author: Ron Wilkinson

reviews.text: It's like Planes, Trains & Automobiles, only with a catastrophic body count.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: It illustrates once again the movie law that the bigger the apocalypse, the less it means.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: It's as dumb as can be, but it's also the epicenter of the sort of thrills that'll have you shouting "geo-whiz!"
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: The 1974 disaster flick Earthquake is notorious for the casting of 52-year-old Ava Gardner as 59-year-old Lorne Greene's daughter, so rest assured there's nothing THAT daft in any aspect of San Andreas.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: Nothing makes sense, yet it's possible to overlook all of this ridiculousness because you're busy rooting for The Rock to save his family.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: San Andreas is a blue ruin of borrowed elements that even The Rock was unable to save.
reviews.author: Jon Espino

reviews.text: There are things on-screen worth looking at, so if that sums up your criteria for a theater-going experience then you're in luck.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: The kind of movie that one watches to clear the mind after a hectic day. [full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Lucero Calderón

reviews.text: This is the worst movie "The Rock" has done in the last few years. [full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Oswaldo Betancourt Lozano

reviews.text: Disaster porn suitable only for fans of the genre. [full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Acuña

reviews.text: Like a tsunami, the special effects are omnipresent and overwhelm the weak story line. They are absolutely, definitely worth the price of admission, regardless of the totally erroneous science. But see it in 2D not the color-muting 3D.
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: Every attempt to develop the plot disappears amid the visual spectacle. [full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jessica Oliva

reviews.text: The earth of San Andreas cleaves itself open to us like the devil's sunroof. Who are we not to leap into the void?
reviews.author: Wesley Morris

reviews.text: The CGI effects in this film, directed by Brad Peyton, are quite remarkable and help take one's mind off the cornball disaster-brings-families-together underpinnings.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: One can fault the film for lacking inventiveness, but in terms of its entertainment quotient, it's an enthralling treat for those who have the appetite to digest mass-destruction in movies.
reviews.author: Mohar Basu

reviews.text: Despite all the exaggerations that will not pass the radar of a geologist and depicting human misery in 3D, the target audience don't need to put their popcorn binge on hold.
reviews.author: Anuj Kumar

reviews.text: San Andreas ticks off all disaster-movie requirements as it runs its characters through a mill of ever-escalating challenges. But if you're looking for a challenging film, San Andreas would itself qualify as a disaster.
reviews.author: Randall King

reviews.text: It may be big, loud, and pretty dumb, but San Andreas is a fun (albeit fleeting) piece of summer blockbuster escapism.
reviews.author: Ben Kendrick

reviews.text: The fault isn't in the earthquake in SAN ANDREAS, it's in the script. Dwayne Johnson's heroics may be able to save everything else in this by-the-numbers disaster (movie), but not that.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Maybe if Giamatti and Johnson had switched roles, we'd have had a full course instead of eye candy for disaster buffs.
reviews.author: Burl Burlingame

reviews.text: [The] visuals are freaky as heck. But they can't distract from a plot that's lazy and kind of offensive, barely batting an eye as thousands perish.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: San Andreas is essentially the filmic equivalent of Disaster Movie Bingo. Well, not entirely. It doesn't have the dog. But the rest is there.
reviews.author: Dominick Suzanne-Mayer

reviews.text: The characters - including Ioan Gruffudd, playing a slimy propetry developer - might be a trifle two-dimensional, but San Francisco has never collapsed so convincingly.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: When the story is as weak as the film's fault lines and the character development never develops, the problem with blowing $100 million mostly on special effects is all you're left with is unintelligent disaster porn.
reviews.author: Adam Fendelman

reviews.text: Hell, I'm as up as the next guy for a dumb summer epic with special effects that fire up audiences. But did San Andreas have to be such a monument to stupidity?
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Over the top, ridiculous, but an acceptable popcorn movie thanks to an amiable cast led by Dwayne Johnson
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: San Andreas doesn't aim very high. It's nothing more than a popcorn movie, designed to offer two hours of mindless thrills. On that level, it's quite passable. Then again, there have got to be some new ideas that disaster movies can be infused with.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Johnson can rappel out of a helicopter and leap from a plane, hotwire a truck and pilot a boat through a tsunami, and even bring someone back from the dead. He's the Rock AND the Man.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: "The death of one man is a tragedy, the death of millions is a statistic," Joseph Stalin is alleged to have said. That philosophy applies very nicely to the modern disaster movie
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: The Rock can't quite save clichéd, violent disaster movie.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Top-notch effects and a bottom-scraping script make this disaster flick a spectacular bore.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: [T]he film never convinces us that these people exist for any reason other than generic stand-ins to be threatened so that we aren't merely watching two hours of footage of buildings falling over.
reviews.author: Mark Hughes

reviews.text: Succeeds at exploiting a proven disaster-movie formula without troubling itself much with little things like plot, character, and dialogue.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: San Andreas doesn't hit a single beat you don't expect, and there's comfort in that.
reviews.author: Will Leitch

reviews.text: San Andreas just wants to show destruction and it wants you to revel in it. That's nearly impossible given the timing of the release and the fact that reveling in nothing but glorified destruction got old at least five years ago.
reviews.author: Matthew Razak

reviews.text: San Andreas may CGI-shake the digital earth, but it's really stray bits inside a hollow shell, and the Dolby howl of the sound design is just to mask the empty rattle of the film, a flimsy shell filled with cliches and summer-dumb spectacle.
reviews.author: James Rocchi

reviews.text: The Rock delivers big, dumb disaster fun. San Andreas asks you to check your brain at the door, sit back, and enjoy CGI buildings toppling like Legos
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: San Andreas is lightweight, crowd-pleasing summer entertainment that knows its place and delivers the goods.
reviews.author: Bill Clark

reviews.text: Objectively, "San Andreas" probably shouldn't work. But you don't enjoy a roller coaster by thinking about it.
reviews.author: Greg Maki

reviews.text: Mid-movie Dwayne Johnson's Ray is told if he can't save his daughter no one can. He saves her but can't save the movie. A disaster of a disaster movie.
reviews.author: Gary Wolcott

reviews.text: seems to have its tongue firmly planted in cheek, screenwriter Carlton Cuse's take...hitting every genre cliche so relentlessly it all adds up to preposterous entertainment.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: There are things in San Andreas that no one would have dreamed of seeing 40 years ago, when Earthquake (with its tacky, plaster-cracking "Sensurround") represented the state of the art. But nothing means anything.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: It's hokey at times, definitely too long for such a thin premise, but "San Andreas" is never jokey, displaying an endearing determination to take catastrophe with the passable seriousness.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: The Rock gets to emote! You better bring some tissues.
reviews.author: Willie Waffle

reviews.text: ...a refreshing but cheesy take on the natural disaster genre.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: I just like seeing skyscrapers, which I loathe, smashed to bits. On this front, San Andreas delivers in spades.
reviews.author: David Sexton

reviews.text: "San Andreas" never pretends to be any less subtle than the Rock's physique. It's a hulking mass of wanton destruction, and a stupid-fun carnival of carnage.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: San Andreas lacks backbone. Between its steroidic CGI and emotionally vacant plot line, the movie is all flex, no muscle.
reviews.author: Julia Cooper

reviews.text: Ridiculous, but often in that guilty-pleasure, disaster-movie sort of way, wherein we all laugh at the portentous cliches.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: Quite literally the blockbuster of the year.
reviews.author: Steven Rea

reviews.text: San Andreas is competently assembled and teeming with impressive spectacle but is also emotionally stale.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: For connoisseurs of unintentionally terrible movies, San Andreas delivers more than a few hearty belly laughs.
reviews.author: Stephen Rebello

reviews.text: I've seen some pretty good comedies lately that didn't make me laugh this hard.
reviews.author: Tim Martain

reviews.text: If all you honestly want out of it is to watch 'stuff blow up good,' you could still do a lot better than this uneven entry in the already overstuffed disaster porn genre.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: This particular disaster film is in shambles and it seems even The Rock cannot rescue it.
reviews.author: Jyoti Sharma Bawa

reviews.text: There's really nothing in San Andreas we haven't seen before in other disaster films, with the exception of The Rock as the hero.
reviews.author: Kirk Baird

reviews.text: Audiences who choose to seek out "San Andreas" will get exactly what they came for. Undeniably silly but riveting when it means it most, the film delivers the goods. Snooty cinephiles need not apply.
reviews.author: Dustin Putman

reviews.text: Schlock disaster porn...disaster as family therapy.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: The Rock, you could say, is caught in a hard place here: lumbered with a powerfully stupid script and drainingly repetitive special effects. But as so often in his career, he makes the best of it.
reviews.author: John Nugent

reviews.text: Nothing is subtle, and Ioan Gruffudd's cowardly tycoon is a copy of Richard Chamberlain's engineer from The Towering Inferno, but Johnson, a human edifice, is more than equal to the preposterous destruction.
reviews.author: Andrew Collins

reviews.text: [A] yawning fun vacuum ...
reviews.author: Adam Woodward

reviews.text: In the end, though, it's like the aftermath of any large earthquake: You'll be glad it wasn't any worse while noticing its many faults.
reviews.author: Christopher Lawrence

reviews.text: Paul Giamatti is perfectly cast as the rumpled scientist and his scenes are by far the most interesting. It causes one to wonder if San Andreas might have worked better if the entire film had focused on his character.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Sure, the CGI and the VFX are impressive, but the characters aren't, and rather than trying to break any sort of new ground, the movie simply churns it up.
reviews.author: Anders Wright

reviews.text: As a helter skelter, fairground ride, San Andreas is often exhilarating but the fault lines in its screenplay become more and more apparent.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: It doesn't bode well when a movie that will sink or swim entirely on its CGI technology can't even manage a convincingly Photoshopped family portrait.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: For all the unabashed cliches and straight-faced silliness delivered by Johnson, Paul Giamatti, and their generally capable castmates, they're doing something right.
reviews.author: Tom Russo

reviews.text: The cringeworthy dialogue and unmoving earnestness are the biggest disasters in this mostly forgettable action flick
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: There are several requirements that must be met by any disaster movie not wanting to qualify as a disaster itself. San Andreas ticks off all the boxes; this doesn't make it a great film, but it does qualify as a fine disaster flick.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Here is a fantastically silly spectacular about San Francisco collapsing into the juddering and shuddering San Andreas fault.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: This is why we can't have nice things.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: San Andreas fulfills its promise of providing massive quantities of disaster. Ultimately, though, we're left wondering if that alone is a promise worth keeping.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The movie values neither human life nor audience entertainment, which is simply a lose/lose situation.
reviews.author: Devin Faraci

reviews.text: Helo-flown and hella-dumb, the movie delivers what its ads promise and not a particle more: Semi-convincing digital erasure of infrastructure.
reviews.author: Chris Klimek

reviews.text: "San Andreas" delivers a collection of harrowing set pieces where the sets inevitably go to pieces.
reviews.author: Jon Niccum

reviews.text: San Andreas does exactly what it set out to do: Satisfy the thrill-seekers with a popcorn movie. If you want something more serious about earthquakes, you have to watch the nightly news.
reviews.author: Bruce Kirkland

reviews.text: Manages to inject enough pathos to stay engaging.
reviews.author: Tony Stamp

reviews.text: When you think about it, is there anybody else you'd want looking out for you in times of trouble than Johnson?
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: When the filmmakers take such mayhem to an absurd level and then pile on the dangers and obstacles, the film finds the right sort of guilty pleasure tone and appeal. (Full Content Review - Sex, Profanity, Violence, etc. - for Parents also available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Hahahaha. Really, that's about all there is to say about "San Andreas" ...
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: It's not the best summer blockbuster you'll see this year, but San Andreas offers solid entertainment thanks to big set pieces, simple storytelling and, of course, Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.
reviews.author: Max Nicholson

reviews.text: An action hero with a rare kind of gravitas, Johnson has a stabilizing influence on all the silliness that surrounds him.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: "San Andreas" changes all too quickly from satisfyingly foolish to dismayingly dumb to genuinely stupid.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: It's all big, distant, unfathomable wreckage - shattering skyscrapers and rippling cityscapes - with no sense of the human cost
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: "San Andreas" plays as if the four screenwriters shopped at the disaster-movie supermarket, grabbing all the clichés they could from the clearance aisle and stuffing them in a cart.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Considered as pure spectacle, "San Andreas" is gripping and effective, as well as a somewhat interesting form of counter-narrative: A vision of near-term apocalypse that has nothing to do with climate change, monsters or alien invaders.
reviews.author: Andrew O'Hehir

reviews.text: Some movies are easy to mock, but hard to resist. This is one of them.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: "San Andreas" is an action film that hits viewers over the head. Again and again. But isn't that exactly why you'd want to go see it?
reviews.author: Kevin C. Johnson

reviews.text: There's enough spectacle and entertainment onscreen to nudge the satisfaction needle in the right direction.
reviews.author: Doris Toumarkine

reviews.text: The movie nicely delivers the computer-generated goods - the destruction of the Golden Gate Bridge is pretty spectacular - and if Johnson doesn't quite make it sing, at least it growls suspensefully.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: Stuff go boom. Stuff go BOOM.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: When the earth is roiling and rippling like an angry ocean, it's an impressive sight. It's when the shaking stops though that San Andreas is a different type of disaster.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: An unabashed throwback to the simple-minded disaster movies of decades ago...[and] a ho-hum affair.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: As patently preposterous, scientifically dubious, and unapologetically corny as director Brad Peyton's orgy of CGI devastation is, its popcorn prophecy of the inevitable is a blast of giddy, disposable fun.
reviews.author: Chris Nashawaty

reviews.text: So who's to find fault with a film about faultlines, where one is simply supposed to revel in the seismocalypse and enjoy the tectonic fury?
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: With a final line of dialogue that will reverberate across the eons as one of the worst in Hollywood history, San Andreas marks itself as a film that's so awful it's actually pretty great.
reviews.author: Marc Savlov

reviews.text: Nice to know that billions of dollars in property damage and the deaths of hundreds of thousands of people took place in San Andreas just so Ray and Emma could avoid a no-fault divorce.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: On the positive side: impressive special effects. On the negative side: pretty much everything else.
reviews.author: Lawrence Toppman

reviews.text: I enjoyed large chunks of San Andreas, largely because the actors give it a full load of sincerity, and there's some bizarrely effective comic relief thanks to Hugo Johnstone-Burt and Art Parkinson as Brits who picked the wrong week to visit the Bay Area.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: The dialogue is inappropriately jocular throughout, which undercuts the genuine terror it attempts to muster.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Silly and stupid, but lots of fun.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: San Andreas is such a programmatic, by-the-numbers film, genre-savvy viewers could practically recite along with the script.
reviews.author: Tasha Robinson

reviews.text: San Andreas is the epitome of a summer blockbuster - hollow and empty on the inside, but for all the script problems, there's plenty of eye-popping industrial carnage to behold.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: What truly ruins "San Andreas" is that a lot happens in the plot that makes no damn sense- and that characters keep making decisions that are all but indefensible.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: "San Andreas" is a disaster - literally.
reviews.author: Joe Neumaier

reviews.text: San Andreas doesn't pretend to be anything other than what it is... VFX-driven disaster porn at its finest.
reviews.author: Jason Zingale

reviews.text: Most natural disaster movies are dated because the effects age so badly. San Andreas is a movie with careful CGI that will still look powerful as the years go by.
reviews.author: Chase Whale

reviews.text: Scary disaster movie, revealing spectacular devastation along the California coastline....
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: The action is bracing, Johnson's performance is solid and, within its extremely narrow parameters, entirely convincing, and Gugino and Daddario are both gritty and attractive. The result is a pretty exemplary popcorn movie.
reviews.author: Glenn Kenny

reviews.text: In San Andreas, The Big One finally hits California, and not even Dwayne Johnson's mutant biceps can keep those infamous tectonic plates from separating.
reviews.author: Rene Rodriguez

reviews.text: Not the highest praise to say it reinvigorates the genre when the genre is "dumb Roland Emmerich movie," but it turns out, watching The Rock's muscles get bigger while Alexandra Daddario's outfits get smaller is a pretty good foil for CGI.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: Pretty scary and only moderately stupid.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: It clocks in at less than two hours, only about half of that taken up with a mix of models, computer-generated effects and various other explosions and loud noises. The other half is people saying and doing stupid things.
reviews.author: Jeff Baker

reviews.text: It's hard to appreciate San Andreas as much more than a series of special effects vistas: impeccably detailed, completely plastic.
reviews.author: Ignatiy Vishnevetsky

reviews.text: It's hard not to shrug, stifle a yawn and reach for the popcorn when the Golden Gate Bridge once again buckles and sways and drops vehicles into the bay.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: A by-the-numbers disaster flick featuring passable special effects, thinly-drawn characters, clunky dialogue and predictable plotting.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: Cornball disaster-porn melodrama... in 3D! Dumb, insulting, and bloodless. It's Hollywood's subconscious death wish brought to life, in more ways than one.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: When you're watching the impossibly charismatic former wrestler on screen, you'll not only forgive the movie around him, you'll want to throw Pulitzers, Nobel Prizes and even Miss World crowns at it.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: Thousands of people may die, but the most important thing is that Ray is reunited with his family.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: In Brad Peyton's San Andreas, the biggest earthquake in recorded history is less natural disaster than divorce negotiation process.
reviews.author: Ed Gonzalez

reviews.text: A disaster.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: San Andreas is predictable fun, but with Johnson swinging in to the rescue it also delivers plenty of muscular thrills.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: In particular, a collapsing car rescue shows creative build, and the fact that a tsunami is not the biggest obstacle in a tsunami sequence shows screenwriter Carlton Cuse worked overtime to provide some clever disasters.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Johnson continues to impress with his roles. He tackles this film head on with a wry smile.
reviews.author: Thomas Derwin

reviews.text: It is relentlessly over the top and relentlessly, ridiculously fun.
reviews.author: Stefan Kyriazis

reviews.text: The special effects aren't bad for a lower-budget ($100 million) blockbuster, though director Brad Peyton and his writers often deploy them in downright laughable ways.
reviews.author: Lou Lumenick

reviews.text: As for the story line, there are faults and cracks aplenty. But "San Andreas" does know where its epicenter must be: overdone, loud, anything-but-realistic and enthusiastic destruction sequences.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: A basic, moderately engrossing old-school disaster movie.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: A fair amount of intelligence has gone into San Andreas -- but not into the extremely corny dialogue, which seems designed to make the audience groan.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: This is a film that's pure scale and spectacle, and in that regard it does exactly what it says on the tin.
reviews.author: Garry McConnachie

reviews.text: You already know what's going to happen, but at least you get to watch Johnson do it.
reviews.author: Kate Erbland

reviews.text: Hugely entertaining, sensational tosh, the sort of thing moving pictures were made for.
reviews.author: Angie Errigo

reviews.text: Does for San Francisco what Jaws did for the Ocean!
reviews.author: Kam Williams

reviews.text: By the end, you will be exhausted by all of the digital destruction, but you'll still somehow want to see more of Dwayne Johnson.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: The disaster sequences are competent; the writing, not so much.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: There's zero tension here. You'll just spend two hours admiring the work of the sound technicians and visual effects artists.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: Compared to Roland Emmerich behemoths it's downright minimalist. That's not a compliment.
reviews.author: Matt Prigge

reviews.text: A less-than-basic disaster film with no emotional weight.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: This film doesn't need a director, which is fortunate because it has Brad Peyton..disaster porn..a listless, heaving mess of a film.
reviews.author: Marshall Fine

reviews.text: At times, San Andreas is so bad it's funny, but most of the time, it's just bad.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Together with cinematographer Steve Yedlin and VFX supervisor Colin Strause, director Brad Peyton achieves a persuasive blending of practical shots and superior CG techniques for the most complex sequences.
reviews.author: Justin Lowe

reviews.text: The film frames [Johnson] like a saviour, and bathes him in so much morning sunlight you have to squint, but as he insists to the news crew on board: "I'm just doing my job, ma'am." That's about the strength of it.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Less a Rock-buster than a quake'n'bake reheat of post-Emmerich basics. The cast's likeable work falls right through the script holes.
reviews.author: Kevin Harley

reviews.text: The very earnest human drama fits awkwardly into the action and isn't helped by some unconvincing performances and weak dialogue.
reviews.author: John Hazelton

reviews.text: California crumbles spectacularly in an action movie that quickly degenerates from blissfully stupid to fatally stupid.
reviews.author: Andrew Barker

reviews.text: As far as disaster movies go, they don't come much better than this: heart-stopping action with ginormous stunts and a story that touches your heart. It also helps to have the rock-solid Dwayne Johnson on your side (pun intended)
reviews.author: Louise Keller

reviews.text: A film that deviates away from sentimentality, and while we may crave more profundity, Peyton's commitment to pure entertainment is unwavering.
reviews.author: Stefan Pape

reviews.text: The special effects may look real but the relationships are made of much less sturdy stuff - it doesn't matter how impressively a building collapses ... if you don't believe the scriptwriter is prepared to kill any of them in the name of tension.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: ... a classic case of spectacle over story that'll largely slip from the memory the second Sia's 'California Dreamin' kicks in over the end credits.
reviews.author: Simon Reynolds

reviews.text: Thankfully, the action set pieces are exciting enough, and come at such a successive clip - "Oh, s-t" may be the film's most repeated line of dialogue - that it's only afterward that you have the chance to pause and ask questions about the plot.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: You spend the entire movie willing the earth to open up beneath their characters' feet and swallow them for the good of humankind.
reviews.author: Ali Gray

reviews.text: I can (and will) nitpick storytelling choices and character development, but those merely wanting "Look out, earthquake!" will get their money's worth.
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: The worst disaster movie since Disaster Movie.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: If you crave Emmerich-esque disaster-porn with a mega body count, there's plenty here to OMG at. But when it comes to character depth or plotting, San Andreas is a sadly familiar wasteland.
reviews.author: Dan Jolin

synopsis: A seemingly ideal day turns disastrous when California's notorious San Andreas fault triggers a devastating, magnitude 9 earthquake, the largest in recorded history. As the Earth cracks open and buildings start to crumble, Ray Gaines (Dwayne Johnson), an LAFD search-and-rescue helicopter pilot, must navigate the destruction from Los Angeles to San Francisco to bring his estranged wife (Carla Gugino) and their only daughter (Alexandra Daddario) to safety.
